title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
text: This article demonstrates the complete native GSEA exchange path. We run a pre-ranked analysis with clusterProfiler::GSEA() and its fgsea backend, serialize the resulting gseaResult with protsea, reconstruct it from JSON, verify the preserved data, and create clusterProfiler/enrichplot figures from the reconstructed object. Reconstruction does not rerun enrichment or permutation testing.

title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
section: Prepare a ranked list and gene sets
text:
Prepare a ranked list and gene sets
The example is deterministic and self-contained. The ranking contains 120 proteins. Two pathways occupy opposite ends of the ranking, while a third contains proteins from both ends.

Codeprotein_ids <- sprintf("protein_%03d", seq_len(120))
ranked_scores <- seq(4, -4, length.out = length(protein_ids))
names(ranked_scores) <- protein_ids

term2gene <- data.frame(
  term = rep(c("TOP_PATHWAY", "BOTTOM_PATHWAY", "BOTH_ENDS"), each = 16),
  gene = c(
    protein_ids[1:16],
    protein_ids[105:120],
    protein_ids[c(1:8, 113:120)]
  )
)

term2name <- data.frame(
  term = c("TOP_PATHWAY", "BOTTOM_PATHWAY", "BOTH_ENDS"),
  name = c("Proteins at the top", "Proteins at the bottom", "Proteins at both ends")
)

title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
text:
Run clusterProfiler with fgsea
by = "fgsea" selects the fgsea backend. The non-default exponent is useful here because the round trip must retain the weighting parameter used to reconstruct the running enrichment score.

Codeset.seed(42)
native <- clusterProfiler::GSEA(
  geneList = ranked_scores,
  exponent = 1.25,
  minGSSize = 5,
  maxGSSize = 30,
  pvalueCutoff = 1,
  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
  TERM2NAME = term2name,
  by = "fgsea",
  seed = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

native@result[, c("ID", "Description", "enrichmentScore", "NES", "p.adjust")]

                           ID            Description enrichmentScore       NES
TOP_PATHWAY       TOP_PATHWAY    Proteins at the top             1.0  3.011268
BOTTOM_PATHWAY BOTTOM_PATHWAY Proteins at the bottom            -1.0 -2.931947
BOTH_ENDS           BOTH_ENDS  Proteins at both ends             0.5  1.505634
                   p.adjust
TOP_PATHWAY    1.500000e-10
BOTTOM_PATHWAY 1.500000e-10
BOTH_ENDS      5.378486e-02

title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
text:
Serialize and deserialize
gsea_result_data() creates the shared R representation. write_gsea_result_json() writes it as JSON for file exchange. The same JSON text can be stored directly in a MuData uns entry and passed to decode_gsea_json() without an intermediate file.

Codedocument <- protsea::gsea_result_data(
  results = list(treatment_vs_control = native),
  category = "Example pathways",
  method = "fgsea"
)

json_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
protsea::write_gsea_result_json(document, json_path)
json_text <- paste(readLines(json_path, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")

restored <- protsea::decode_gsea_json(json_text)[["treatment_vs_control"]][["Example pathways"]]

data.frame(
  Property = c("Result table", "Ranked list", "Gene sets", "GSEA parameters"),
  Equivalent = c(
    isTRUE(all.equal(restored@result, native@result)),
    isTRUE(all.equal(restored@geneList, native@geneList)),
    isTRUE(all.equal(restored@geneSets, native@geneSets)),
    isTRUE(all.equal(restored@params, native@params))
  )
)

         Property Equivalent
1    Result table       TRUE
2     Ranked list       TRUE
3       Gene sets       TRUE
4 GSEA parameters       TRUE


The JSON retains the complete typed result table, ordered ranking, complete gene sets, leading-edge identifiers, and the actual analysis parameters with their R storage types. This is enough for enrichplot to derive hit positions and running-score curves from the reconstructed object.

title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
text:
Plot the reconstructed result
The following plots use restored, not the original native object.

Codeenrichplot::dotplot(restored, showCategory = 3) +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Reconstructed GSEA result")






Figure 1: Normalized enrichment scores and adjusted p-values reconstructed from JSON.





Codeenrichplot::ridgeplot(restored, showCategory = 3) +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Rank distributions after JSON round trip")






Figure 2: Rank-score distributions for the reconstructed pathway memberships.





Codeenrichplot::gseaplot2(
  restored,
  geneSetID = c("TOP_PATHWAY", "BOTTOM_PATHWAY"),
  title = "Running enrichment scores after JSON round trip"
)






Figure 3: Running enrichment scores reconstructed from the retained ranking, gene sets, and exponent.

title: clusterProfiler GSEA JSON round trip
section: What the JSON round trip supports
text:
What the JSON round trip supports
The native round trip retains ES, NES, raw and adjusted p-values, q-values, result-table types, full gene-set membership, leading edges, exact rank order including ties, and the weighting exponent. Permutation matrices are deliberately omitted because this format supports result exchange and plotting rather than resuming permutation calculations.

title: protsea
text:
Extends the STRING data / rank_lists structure with a category-level gsea_result block containing native statistics, gene sets and parameters. The pool’s integer rank preserves input order, including tied scores. Every native block also stores the running enrichment score and one-based hit positions for each term. These fields have the same representation for every producer. Identifiers are retained exactly as submitted; no biological ID mapping is performed. Permutation matrices are not stored.



gsea_result_data(results, category, method = "fgsea")







results


Named list of DOSE::gseaResult objects, one per contrast.




category


Gene-set collection name.




method


Algorithm label, e.g. “fgsea” or “DOSE”.






A list with data and rank_lists, suitable for MuData uns or write_gsea_result_json().

text:
Constructs a DOSE::gseaResult suitable for enrichplot::ridgeplot() and other GSEA-specific visualisations. Native gsea_result extensions restore the original statistics. title: protsea
text:
Merges enrichResult objects across contrasts (for a single category) into a DOSE::compareClusterResult object. This enables cross-contrast comparison plots from enrichplot (e.g., dotplot(), emapplot()).

build_compareClusterResult(result_list)




result_list


Named list of DOSE::enrichResult objects, one per contrast. Names are used as cluster labels.


A DOSE::compareClusterResult object.


library("protsea")

results <- read_gsea_json("gsea_result.json")
# Extract GO Process from each contrast
go_list <- lapply(results, function(x) x[["GO Process"]])
ccr <- build_compareClusterResult(go_list)
enrichplot::dotplot(ccr, showCategory = 10)

title: protsea 0.1.0
text:
protsea 0.1.0

Store per-term source running enrichment scores and one-based hit positions in the shared native GSEA block, including documents produced by GSEApy MEA, while reconstructing the same transient clusterProfiler object for plotting.
Keep the single round-trip vignette visible in the generated website’s Articles navigation.
Add a Quarto vignette demonstrating an fgsea-backed clusterProfiler analysis, JSON serialization and reconstruction, equality checks, and plots made from the reconstructed result. Build package documentation with altdoc’s Quarto website backend.
Build the compact round-trip article as the package vignette. Ship GSEA_report.qmd as an installed runtime report template without executing its 112 MB example during every vignette or documentation build.
Construct DOSE result classes from their registered definitions, supporting releases where those S4 classes are not namespace exports.
Promote the STRING JSON readers, plotting conversions, and report templates from stringdbpy/stringGSEAplot into the standalone protsea package.
Write clusterProfiler GSEA results to the existing JSON structure with native statistics, complete gene sets, ranking order, and parameters; reconstruct running-score plots after serialization.
Stop deriving artificial NES values from STRING FDR values.

title: protsea
text:
Documentation and vignette
Shared enrichment JSON and clusterProfiler plotting conversions, extracted from stringdbpy/stringGSEAplot (source commit 7032a69). Install with make install; run tests with make test. Report QMD sources live in vignettes/ and are built and installed with the package.


document <- protsea::gsea_result_data(
  list(treatment_vs_control = result), # clusterProfiler::GSEA() result
  category = "PTMSEA"
)
json <- as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(document, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = NA, na = "null"))
# Store json directly in MuData uns; no intermediate file is required.
restored <- protsea::decode_gsea_json(json)$treatment_vs_control$PTMSEA
enrichplot::gseaplot2(restored, geneSetID = 1)
For standalone file exchange, use write_gsea_result_json(document, path) and decode_gsea_json(path). Existing STRING files remain readable through read_gsea_json(path), returning nested enrichResult objects; build_compareClusterResult() supports cross-contrast plots.



The common document retains data[contrast] (a shared gene_pool and categories) and rank_lists[contrast].entries. STRING metadata and links are optional. Term fields remain compatible with stringdbpy and PTM consumers. leading_edge_ids carries the leading subset separately from full mapped gene_ids.
For clusterProfiler results, each category additionally contains gsea_result:







Field
Content




result.columns, result.types, result.row_names
Original result table, including ES, NES, raw p-value, adjusted p-value, q-value, leading edge and any backend-specific columns; empty columns retain their types.


gene_sets
Complete original gene sets, including members absent from the ranking.


params, param_types
Original analysis parameters and their R storage types, including the actual weighting exponent.


running_scores
Per-term running enrichment-score vectors in ranked-list order.


hit_indices
Per-term one-based positions of gene-set members in the ranked list.


organism, set_type, key_type, readable, gene2symbol
Identifier and collection metadata required by the reconstructed object.



Every ranked input is in the pool. Its integer rank determines the exact original order, including ties; input_label addresses the original identifier in rank_lists.entries. Object-key ordering and display labels are never used to determine the native ranking. PTM-specific canonical pool identifiers may differ from input_label without losing the submitted identifiers.
The original enrichment_score field keeps its existing producer-specific meaning: STRING’s score for STRING output and NES for native PTM/GSEA output. Exact native statistics are unambiguous in gsea_result.result.columns.enrichmentScore, NES, pvalue, and p.adjust. Consumers needing those statistics should decode that block instead of interpreting the legacy summary field.
Reconstruction restores gseaResult without re-running enrichment. The common native block records source running scores and hit positions for direct comparison, while enrichplot can independently reproduce them from the retained ranks, gene sets and exponent. Permutation matrices are omitted; the exchange format supports reporting, not resuming permutation calculations. JSON uses full numeric precision and null for missing table values.
STRING documents without a native block remain valid common documents. STRING does not provide native fgsea NES or raw p-values; its plotting adapter leaves those statistics missing. The STRING ridgeplot remains a descriptive view of mapped members, and decode_gsea_json() rejects documents without the native inputs rather than inventing them. Native MEA producers use the same block as fgsea producers and retain the exact GSEApy running scores and hit positions.
The STRING report can be rendered from the installed package through render_gsea_reports(). PTM report templates remain in prophosqua.
